definitions.explanation: Describes something that is thick and substantial in flesh or material, often used for food items like meat, fish, or vegetables with a satisfying thickness.

examples.japanese: {肉厚|にくあつ}な⟦ステーキ→ステーキ：01369_suteeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{椎茸|しいたけ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{肉厚|にくあつ}で{食|た}べ{応|ごた}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: These shiitake mushrooms are thick and satisfying to eat.

examples.japanese: {肉厚|にくあつ}な⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{皿|さら}→皿：00883_sara⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦たっぷり→たっぷり：03404_tappuri⟧⟦{盛|も}られていた→盛る：00292_moru⟧。
examples.english: Thick-cut sashimi was generously piled on a large plate.

notes:
Literally 'flesh-thick' (⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧ flesh/meat + {厚|あつ} thick). Primarily used to describe food that is satisfyingly thick or fleshy, but can also be used for leaves, fabrics, and other materials.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肉厚|にくあつ}な⟦ステーキ→ステーキ：01369_suteeki⟧: thick steak
- {肉厚|にくあつ}な{椎茸|しいたけ}: thick shiitake mushrooms
- {肉厚|にくあつ}な⟦{切|き}り{身|み}→切り身：21110_kirimi⟧: thick fillet
- {肉厚|にくあつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: fleshy leaves (of a succulent, etc.)

USAGE:
Almost always used as a positive descriptor, implying quality, substance, and satisfaction. Very common in food reviews, restaurant descriptions, and cooking contexts. Can function as a な-adjective ({肉厚|にくあつ}な) or as a noun referring to the thickness of the flesh/material ({肉厚|にくあつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{分厚|ぶあつ}い→分厚い：10502_buatsui⟧: thick — general thickness for books, slices, etc.; not specific to flesh
- ⟦{厚|あつ}い→厚い：00690_atsui⟧: thick — the basic adjective for thickness
- ⟦ボリューム→ボリューム：27002_boryuumu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: voluminous, substantial — more casual, applies to portion size broadly
